**Swift connects Bizum, PayID and Pix for cross-border alias payments**

*Consumers in Spain, Australia and Brazil can now send money internationally using a mobile number or email, a model that could extend to other domestic schemes and reshape cross-border retail payments.*

Swift has launched a cross-border gateway that connects domestic instant payment schemes, starting with Spain's Bizum, Australia's PayID and Brazil's Pix. The service lets consumers send money internationally using an alias such as a mobile number or email address rather than account details, layering a familiar domestic experience onto correspondent banking rails.

The initiative uses existing Swift payment messages and correspondent banking infrastructure rather than requiring new settlement arrangements. That pragmatic approach distinguishes it from more ambitious interoperability projects such as mBridge or Project Nexus, which aim to bypass correspondent banking altogether. By working with what already exists, Swift can move faster, though the trade-off is that it inherits the cost and latency characteristics of correspondent banking.

The inclusion of Bizum is the most immediate signal for Europe. If the model works, other European schemes including Wero could follow, giving Swift a route into the retail instant payments layer it has historically left to domestic operators. Domestic schemes, which have built their brands on speed and simplicity, face a strategic question about whether they will accept the friction that cross-border correspondent banking inevitably introduces.

*Sources: [Swift provides cross-border gateway to Bizum, PayID and Pix users](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48488/swift-provides-cross-border-gateway-to-bizum-payid-and-pix-users?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.original:
**ECB invites private sector to join digital euro innovation platform**

*The call for expressions of interest opens a formal channel for companies to shape value-added services on the digital euro, moving the project beyond policy design into practical product development.*

The European Central Bank is inviting private companies and organisations to join the digital euro innovation platform, where participants will collaborate on experiments with new value-added services and explore future technological developments. The call marks a shift from the closed pilot phase, which selected 36 payment providers in July, toward broader private-sector engagement on what the digital euro can actually do beyond basic person-to-person and point-of-sale payments.

Legislative momentum is running in parallel. The European Parliament's July vote to advance the digital euro regulation to final negotiations has given the ECB room to ensure commercial applications are ready when, or if, the political process concludes. The innovation workstreams are designed to surface use cases that justify the digital euro's existence to consumers and merchants who already have functioning payment options.

The ECB faces persistent scepticism from commercial banks and payment providers who view the digital euro as a competitor rather than a complement. Bringing private firms inside the development process is partly a technical exercise and partly a political one, aimed at building the coalition needed to make the digital euro viable at launch.

*Sources: [ECB invites expressions of interest for digital euro innovation workstreams](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48490/ecb-invites-expressions-of-interest-for-digital-euro-innovation-workstreams?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**European banks struggling to match fraud checks with instant payment speeds**

*Payment professionals rank the instant payments regulation and verification of payee as bigger compliance challenges than the EU AI Act, as banks scramble to align fraud controls with real-time settlement under the instant payments regulation.*

European banks are finding it difficult to run effective fraud screening at the speeds required by instant payments, according to a survey by identity verification firm Sumsub. Payment practitioners ranked the instant payments regulation (cited by 27% of respondents) and verification of payee (26%) as their most pressing compliance challenges, ahead of the EU AI Act (21%) and the EU anti-money laundering regulation (22%).

The findings quantify a problem that has been building since the instant payments regulation took effect. Banks that previously had hours or days to flag suspicious transactions now have seconds, and legacy screening systems were not designed for that tempo. Verification of payee, which the European Payments Council is still rolling out unevenly across the single euro payments area, is intended to catch misdirected and fraudulent payments before they settle, but delays in implementation have left gaps that fraudsters exploit.

For operational teams inside European banks, the immediate challenge of keeping fraud controls aligned with real-time settlement is more urgent than the broader regulatory questions posed by AI or AML harmonisation. That aligns with warnings from banking associations in July that instant payment speeds were outpacing real-time monitoring capabilities.

*Sources: [European Banks Struggling to Catch Fraud at Instant Payment Speeds, Finds Sumsub](https://financialit.net/news/payments/european-banks-struggling-catch-fraud-instant-payment-speeds-finds-sumsub) — Financialit*

**BNY launches pay-to-wallet capability for cross-border bank transfers**

*Banks can now route cross-border payments directly into retail digital wallets using existing Swift infrastructure, targeting the growing population of consumers who hold balances in wallets rather than traditional bank accounts.*

BNY has launched a pay-to-wallet capability that enables banks to send cross-border payments from bank accounts directly into participating retail digital wallets. The service uses existing Swift payment messages and correspondent banking infrastructure, avoiding the need for new settlement or clearing arrangements.

Remittance recipients in many markets, particularly in emerging economies, increasingly hold funds in digital wallets rather than bank accounts. Sending money from a bank account to a wallet has typically required the recipient to withdraw from a bank account into the wallet, adding a step, a delay and often a fee. BNY's service removes that intermediary step for participating wallets.

The launch sits alongside Swift's own move to connect domestic payment aliases cross-border, announced the same day. Together, the two initiatives suggest that the correspondent banking layer is actively adapting to compete with newer cross-border rails such as stablecoin networks and bilateral instant payment links. European banks that rely on BNY as a correspondent gain a distribution channel they can offer corporate clients sending payroll or supplier payments to wallet-heavy markets.

*Sources: [BNY unveils Pay-to-Wallet technology option for banks](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48487/bny-unveils-pay-to-wallet-technology-option-for-banks?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
